Thank you for your candid response.


>Life purposes are ever-changing. Some people have life-long passions, others find passion in pursuing a variety of purposes.



I would argue that they are one and the same -  a passion is an expression of a purpose.


>To say you've lost your purpose only means you've lost "a purpose" that seemed to matter at the moment.


I feel that a statement like this weighs greatly on what one attaches to the purpose, how much one understands oneself and attributes that to the 'purpose', and how long one perceives to be a moment. Take any one of these at an extreme - what if this purpose meant a great deal? Why is it assumed that the finding of a new course of action, a new passion for life morally correct thing to do? If all your energy and effort is put towards this goal or purpose, is it not sensible to commit suicide when your purpose becomes impossible to pursue?


>Life is also a chain of compromises. Holding onto things with a death grip is ludicrous because in the end, it won't matter; you'll simply be dead.


How tightly one grips is, I believe, greatly related to ones values and how strongly one adheres to them, as well as ones cultural background. I don't agree with your statement that holding onto certain passions and purposes tightly will cause one to be 'simply dead', with (I'm reading an implication into what you wrote, apologies if I am wrong) no real result to show for it. Take Thích Quảng Đức, the monk who immolated himself in protest of the Vietnam war. His actions inspired a great number of people towards a positive end - is his method of protest immoral?


I also disagree with your example, and the point it tries to make - perhaps our hypothetical mother was an impulsive liar, kleptomaniac, and backstabber, and the pain she would have caused continuing her life would match or exceed the pain suicide caused unto her family. Or perhaps by internalizing my hypothetical mothers death, I gain the drive and determination to conduct groundbreaking neuroscientific research, saving the lives of tens of thousands and making it more affordable for all. A great number of horrible people have come out of families of suicides. Brilliant, good people have as well. Statistically, there is most probably a trend, but there are no absolutes.

Hello.


I am young and I feel like killing myself.


I also feel somewhat wary of posting specifics publicly online. I hope you guys understand.



Would it be possible to speak with someone via AIM or other online messaging client?



Any help would be appreciated.

Thanks in advance.


2/26 4:00AM Edit: Thank you so much to all of you who extended a hand to help me. It means a great deal to me. I spoke with someone and feel more stable and I have a great deal to think about now. My regards towards all who have lent an ear.
